name: slider
title: Slider
description: Choose a value, or a range of two, along a bounded track.

base.summary: The track, the fill and the row they sit in. The drawn track is decoration over a transparent native input, so these measurements are what the reader sees, not what they touch.

tokens.hit area block-size: size.control.sm — the transparent input's height, and so the touch target, regardless of the drawn thumb
tokens.track background: theme.border.strong — the boundary tone tuned to the 3:1 WCAG 1.4.11 asks of a control (decision C8). Progress's track is theme.bg.muted because a progress bar reports status; a slider's empty track is part of an interactive control and says how far the value can still go, so it has to be seen
tokens.fill background: theme.accent-role.bg — from min to the thumb, or between the two thumbs of a range
tokens.output font-variant: tabular-nums, so the number does not shift width as it changes

thumb.summary: The drawn handle. Surface-filled with an accent edge, so it reads against both the fill and the empty track it travels between.

tokens.inline-size / block-size: size.icon.md — the checkbox box's size, so a slider and a checkbox in one settings column carry the same visual weight
tokens.hover / press: compose the .rata-state-layer class, triggered by the data-hovered and data-pressed attributes the primitive sets (decision C9)
tokens.focus ring: focus.ring-width solid theme.focus-ring, offset focus.ring-offset, drawn on the thumb when the input matches :focus-visible
tokens.movement: transform, not a layout property, with no transition while dragging — a thumb that lags the finger reads as broken

behavior.summary: One or two native range inputs over a drawn track, composed with Field for the label and helper text. APG Slider and Multi-Thumb Slider, with the platform supplying the keyboard model and the touch-screen-reader gestures a scripted slider cannot receive.

decisions.decision: It is built on native `<input type="range">`, one per thumb, not a `div role="slider"`
decisions.why: The APG Slider and Multi-Thumb Slider patterns describe `role="slider"` on any element, and both are satisfied by a native range input, which brings things a div cannot: iOS VoiceOver's swipe-to-adjust, which fires no key events and so never reaches a scripted slider; form participation; and the platform's keyboard model including Home, End and PageUp/PageDown. A range is two inputs sharing a track, each its own tab stop with its own name — which is what the multi-thumb pattern asks for anyway.

decisions.decision: The native input is the hit surface; the track and thumb are drawn
decisions.why: A range input's thumb is a pseudo-element, styled differently in every engine and unable to carry a class. So the input is laid over the drawn track at full size and transparent, receiving every pointer, touch and key event, while the visible thumb is a real element positioned from the value. The hit area is the input's block-size, size.control.sm, independent of the drawn thumb's size — 2.5.8's target minimum met without a thumb that looks swollen.

decisions.decision: The thumb composes `.rata-state-layer`, which will also respond to `[data-hovered]` and `[data-pressed]`
decisions.why: The state layer reacts to `:hover` and `:active` on the element carrying the class, but here the element under the pointer is the transparent input and the element that shows the feedback is the drawn thumb. A `:has(input:hover)` rule would be the hand-rolled hover this system forbids. So `.rata-state-layer` is to be extended to respond to `[data-hovered]` and `[data-pressed]` as well, set by the slider primitive from pointer events on the input, and the thumb composes the class like any other control — identical feedback, with state.hover-opacity and state.press-opacity unchanged; only the trigger widens. That extension is a state-layer change in its own gated step, not part of this contract, and the slider cannot ship before it does (decision C9, docs/decisions/2026-11-gate-1-review.md).

decisions.decision: Track tone is split from Progress by role; track thickness is one shared token, still to be proposed
decisions.why: A slider's track belongs to an interactive control, so it takes theme.border.strong, which meets the 3:1 WCAG 1.4.11 asks of a control's boundary. Progress's track is a status mark, the recessed well theme.bg.muted is documented for, and keeps that tone. The two contracts had disagreed about thickness too; they now share one track-thickness token, proposed through the design-tokens interview (Purpose / Use when / Don't use for / Pairs with) rather than written ad hoc. Until it is approved the recipe holds space.1 as a placeholder, named as one so it is not shipped quietly (decision C8, docs/decisions/2026-11-gate-1-review.md).

decisions.decision: A single pointer can always reach any value without dragging
decisions.why: WCAG 2.5.7 requires an alternative to dragging. Pressing anywhere on the track moves the nearest thumb there, which the native input already does, and is kept on purpose rather than suppressed for a drag-only feel.

A vertical slider on the web is a rotated input with a different keyboard direction, it fights vertical page scroll on touch, and every case seen so far — volume, zoom — is better served horizontally in the layouts this system builds. The track sets `touch-action: pan-y` so a horizontal drag adjusts while a vertical swipe still scrolls the page. Vertical can be added as an `orientation` prop when something needs it; it should not be paid for before.

Change fires on every pointer move, and the commonest bug with sliders is a query per pixel. Commit fires once per interaction — release, keypress or AT adjustment — so the expensive work has a correct place to go that does not require the caller to build a debounce and guess its delay.

A slider always holds a value between `min` and `max` on the `step` grid, so there is no invalid state to show and no unanswered one to require. A constraint across two fields belongs to the form, which can report it in a Notice.

decisions.decision: No tick marks or labelled stops in this version
decisions.why: Marks look simple and carry three decisions: whether they snap, how their labels avoid colliding at narrow widths, and whether they are announced. A discrete scale is served meanwhile by `step` plus `formatValue` returning the stop's name, which gets the announcement right — the part that matters most.

No primitive exists yet. The proposal returns the input, drawn-thumb, track and output prop bags for one or two thumbs, keeps two thumbs from crossing (each thumb's `min`/`max` is the other's value), snaps to `step`, implements the disabled guard described under `disabled`, and sets the `data-hovered` and `data-pressed` attributes the extended state layer responds to (decision C9).

Web: one `<input type="range">` per thumb, with `aria-valuetext` from `formatValue` and `aria-label` from `thumbLabels` on a range, inside a Field; a range is a `role="group"` labelled by `label`. Pointer, touch and keyboard all go through the native input. React Native: core no longer ships a Slider (it moved to a community package), and taking that dependency would make every native consumer install it, so the native component is a `View` driven by the responder system with `accessibilityRole="adjustable"`, `accessibilityValue={{ min, max, now, text }}` — `text` from `formatValue` — and `accessibilityActions` for increment and decrement, which is what VoiceOver's and TalkBack's swipe gestures call. A range is two adjustable views. `onValueCommit` maps to responder release and to each accessibility action. `name` is web-only. Rata-drawn (decision N5): React Native core has no slider any more and the community one cannot be styled to the recipe, so native draws the track and thumb itself rather than using an OS control. The native implementation ships in the pro tier (decision N6).

label.summary: What the value measures. Always required — `labelHidden` hides it, nothing removes it.
use: The quantity, with its unit when the output does not carry one: "Volume", "Max price (USD)".
dont: A sentence. It is read before every value change a screen reader announces.
label.a11y: Bound to the input by Field, so it is the slider's accessible name. For a range it names the group, and each thumb is named by `thumbLabels`.

value.summary: Controls the value from outside. A two-element tuple renders two thumbs.
use: A filter that other controls also write to, or a value persisted elsewhere.
dont: Passing it alongside `defaultValue`. One of them owns the state.
Switching between a number and a tuple across renders. The number of thumbs is decided once.

defaultValue.summary: The starting value when the component owns the state. Its shape decides one thumb or two.
use: `[min, max]` for a range filter that starts unconstrained.
dont: A value off the `step` grid. It is snapped on the first interaction, which looks like the control jumped by itself.

onValueChange.summary: Fires continuously while the thumb moves.
use: Updating the visible output and anything cheap that should track the thumb.
dont: A network request. A drag fires this dozens of times a second — that is `onValueCommit`.

onValueCommit.summary: Fires once when an interaction ends: pointer release, a key press, or an assistive-technology adjustment.
use: Re-running a query or saving a preference — anything expensive enough that it should happen once per decision.
dont: Assuming it follows a drag only. Each arrow-key press is a complete interaction and commits.

use: The real floor of the quantity, not a guess at the usual one.
The real ceiling. If there is none, this is the wrong control — a slider needs both ends to mean anything; use `NumberField`.

step.summary: The grid values snap to. Arrow keys move one step, PageUp and PageDown ten.
use: A step that makes every reachable value meaningful — a price filter in 5s, not in cents.
dont: So fine a step that the thumb cannot land on a chosen value by touch. A hundred steps across a phone-width track is about the limit; past it, add a `NumberField` beside the slider.

thumbLabels.summary: Names for the two thumbs of a range. Required when the value is a tuple.
use: "Minimum price" and "Maximum price" — each thumb is its own control and needs its own name.
dont: Setting it on a single-thumb slider. There is one control and `label` already names it.
thumbLabels.a11y: Each becomes its thumb's `aria-label`, and the group keeps `label`. Without it a reader hears two identical sliders and cannot tell which end they are moving.

formatValue.summary: Turns a value into the text shown in the output and announced as `aria-valuetext`.
use: Units and currency: `(v) => `$${v}``, or `Intl.NumberFormat` for the page's locale.
Named stops on a discrete scale: `(v) => ["Off", "Low", "High"][v]`.
dont: Rounding away the step. The text announced has to be the value the reader will get.
formatValue.a11y: Without it a screen reader announces the bare number, which is meaningless for a price, a percentage or a named level.

showValue.summary: Renders the current value as visible text beside the label.
use: Almost always. A slider without a number is a guess, and touch makes it a worse one — the finger covers the thumb.
dont: Turning it off because the value is shown elsewhere and then not tying the two together. If you hide it, the value has to be visible somewhere the reader is looking.
showValue.a11y: Rendered in an `<output>` tied to the input, but not a live region: the input's own `aria-valuetext` is already announced on every change, and a live output would say it twice.

name.summary: Form field name. A range submits two values under the same name, lower first.

labelHidden.summary: Takes the label off screen while leaving it in the accessibility tree.
use: A control whose meaning is already carried by a heading or column header directly above it.
dont: Pairing it with a placeholder standing in for the name. The placeholder is gone on the first keystroke.
labelHidden.a11y: Field's, unchanged: the label element is still rendered and still bound. Only the pixels go.

id.summary: Stable id for the slider, when something outside needs to point at it.
use: A form library that addresses fields by id, or an error summary linking to the field it names.
dont: Reusing one across two fields. Every id under it — description, message, popup — is derived from this.

description.summary: Persistent helper text under the control.
use: What the value affects, when the label alone does not say: "Applies to new uploads only."
dont: Repeating the label in a sentence. It is read out after the name, so a restatement is heard twice.
description.a11y: Joins `aria-describedby` ahead of the message, so a constraint is heard before a failure.

disabled.summary: Blocks adjustment while keeping the slider focusable, readable and announced.
use: A setting that depends on another being on.
dont: Assuming the value is withheld. It still submits — the same consequence the text field documents.
disabled.a11y: `aria-disabled` on each thumb. A range input has no `readOnly`, so the primitive blocks the change itself: keys and pointer down are refused, and an assistive-technology adjustment that slips past them is reverted to the current value.

className.summary: Class for the wrapper — the width the layout wants, not a restyle.
use: The inline size of the track, which is the layout's decision.
dont: Restyling the thumb or track. They are drawn from the recipe, and the thumb's hit area is sized for touch.

usage.when: A setting with a real floor and ceiling, where the approximate position matters more than the exact number.
usage.notes: `formatValue` is what makes the announcement "40%" rather than "40". The visible output uses the same text, so what is heard and what is seen cannot disagree.

usage.when: Two ends of one interval, adjusted independently.
usage.example:
<Slider
  label="Price"
  defaultValue={[0, 500]}
  max={500}
  step={10}
  thumbLabels={["Minimum price", "Maximum price"]}
  formatValue={(v) => `$${v}`}
  onValueCommit={applyFilter}
/>
usage.notes: `onValueCommit` re-runs the query once per decision rather than once per pixel. `thumbLabels` is required for a tuple: without it a screen reader hears two identical sliders.

usage.case: A discrete scale with named stops
usage.when: A handful of levels with names rather than numbers.
usage.notes: Consider whether this wants to be a `SegmentedControl` instead. Three named options that are all visible at once are easier to choose between than a thumb whose stops are invisible.

usage.when: The reader knows the exact number they want.
usage.notes: Don't. Landing a thumb on 347 out of 1000 by touch is a dexterity test. An exact number is a `NumberField`; if the approximate position also helps, put one beside the other bound to the same value.
